title: Incidental Note

illustrates.quote: Use 7-5 margins for a note without a heading.

blocks.features: Bold heading on a torn-paper-style graphic box.

blocks.text: Why do you think Pericles thought it was so important to beautify and rebuild Athens after the destruction caused by war?
For more information, go online to Meet the People at www.sfsocialstudies.com.
blocks.features: Boxed incidental note with a small computer icon, no heading of its own; a page number '257' is printed at the bottom-right corner of the graphic (page furniture, not transcribed).

print.notes: Illustrates 9.6.1e (a note without a heading, using 7-5 margins): unlike Example 9-7, this note has no heading of its own, so the whole note block uses a first-line/runover 7-5 pattern.
print.surroundingText: Textbook page discussion question about Pericles and the rebuilding of Athens.
print.printFeatures: Torn-paper-style graphic box with a bold heading and a discussion question, plus a separate small boxed incidental note (with a computer icon) referring the reader to a companion website.

braille.notes: Measured fixed left margin = 8 ASCII spaces, stripped. Line 1 (heading) indent 4 (cell 5); lines 2-4 (discussion-question paragraph) indent 0 (cell 1); line 5 blank; line 6 (incidental note, first line) indent 6 (cell 7); line 7 (note runover) indent 4 (cell 5) -- the 7-5 margin pattern of 9.6.1e for a note without its own heading; line 8 blank, per 9.6.1c. Unlike Examples 9-4/9-7, this block's own leading position (source .txt line 6821) is the heading's first line directly, with no separate leading all-blank-cell line before it -- confirmed against the source: lines 6817-6820 are truly-empty .txt filler (page-layout gap), not a margin+blank-cells content line.

resolution: A and B transcribed identical `braille.lines`, verified byte-for-byte against lines 6821-6828 after stripping the measured 8-space margin. Both runs agreed the whole note (including the page number '257') is page furniture except the quoted note text. `illustrates.rule` narrowed to 9.6.1.e specifically (both runs cited the whole of 9.6.1) since this example -- unlike Example 9-7, which has a note heading and illustrates 9.6.1d -- shows a note with NO heading of its own, the specific case named in clause e. Heading level 2 (cell 5) measured directly from the agreed braille's own 4-cell indent, matching example-9-7's own heading-level convention.
